body:
**Credit name.** Amund Kristiansen (GitHub @amundsk).

**Claim.** One new upper bound. The side is the certificate's exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places.

| n | New upper bound | Best public before it | Improvement | That bound's source |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 303 | 17.909762327476 | 17.909772217275 | 9.89e-6 | Evan Daniel (#728; the register) |

Comparison: the register (`packing/frontier/n-303.md` on `main`, checked 2026-10-23) and the open issues and pull
requests that mention 303 (#375, #470, #573, #593, #719, PR #574); the smallest of those is 17.909958291070 (PR #574).

**Certificate.** Gist https://gist.github.com/amundsk/78f9f0e7b4669f2f509a281845081768 at revision `511f56bf6e6afb4eb22f12d31371c2a2fe7b4767`:

| file | S′ (certificate side) | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `s303_amund.cert` | 223872029093440709529093216833/12500000000000000000000000000 = 17.909762327475256427… | `9ec01059b35cc983cb28a1bb33bd215a2717228f7efd182e1724de6b22dc511b` |
| `s303_amund.input.txt` | (float64, side 17.909762327457347) | `19fc5d171a26bf8d4a925c0457fa367b12127e8bd581d91c6dcd573108e4bba4` |

It is a dilation certificate made with Evan Daniel's `search/packer/dilate_cert.py` (evand/square-packing at
`7982d7a9346e29e36cab3ce075274f3023114353`): the float64 packing's centres and box scaled by 1 + 10⁻¹², coordinates
rounded to rationals and each angle to a rational half-angle tangent, so every square is exactly unit. It certifies
the upper bound only.

**Checking.**
- `search/exact/verify_cert.py` (separating axes, exact rational, standard library only) from evand/square-packing at
  `7982d7a9346e29e36cab3ce075274f3023114353`: `VALID: s(n) <= S`; min wall clearance 8.2e-13, min pair separation
  1.2e-12 (724 close pairs by separating axes, the rest by disc separation); 0.8 s on a laptop.
  `python3 search/exact/verify_cert.py s303_amund.cert`
- `search/exact/verify_cert2.py` (polygon intersection, exact rational) at the same commit: `VALID: 303 closed unit
  squares pairwise disjoint inside the open box of side 17.909762327475256427 (724 close pairs checked)`; 1.8 s.
  `python3 search/exact/verify_cert2.py s303_amund.cert`
- A third, unpublished exact check (a local packing workbench's rational certifier on the float packing, separate
  code) also accepts it.

**What the checkers share.** The two public checkers share an author (Evan Daniel) and the certificate format, and the
certificate was made with his `dilate_cert.py`; their geometry tests differ. Neither is ours.

**Not done.** No exact KKT solve or local-optimality / rigidity analysis of this packing; the float packing is a
converged polish, not an exact stationary point. Only the upper bound is claimed.

**Lineage and credit.** A new packing found from Evan Daniel's registered packing (#728, W-known-best-n303), not a
refinement of it: the search used non-shrink moves (random kicks, local melts, re-seated squares and rotated patches),
and the result differs in structure. Matched one-to-one against that packing (optimal assignment on centres): max move
0.547, 12 squares move more than 0.1, 31 more than 0.01; tilted squares 96 vs 91; exact sides differ by 9.9e-6.
The search: 2,048 perturbed variants of the register packing per round, relaxed in a GPU batch (Apple Metal, float32)
through a box shrinking slightly below the record side, the best 64 polished in 64-bit with Evan Daniel's `fq`
quench (augmented Lagrangian + SLP, evand/square-packing), then repeated from the current best (an iterated hill
climb; the improvement came in its first pass and again in round 10). Credit: Amund Kristiansen; the polish engine,
certificate generator and checkers are Evan Daniel's.

**AI assistance.** Yes. The search, the certificate and this report were done by Claude (Anthropic), working in Claude
Code at my direction, using Evan Daniel's open-source engine and checkers.
